text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: router fallback loop + dedicated-pool autoscale anomaly. Impacting requests using routing-policy 'cost-fallback-v2' in us-west-2. Error rate spiked ~3m ago, 8% 5xx for affected routes. Pager: oncall-alex

oncall-alex: Paging in. I saw the alert, pulling logs now. Anyone on call for dedicated pool scaling?

runtime-ryan: I’m on. quick summary from metrics: router's fallback policy started sending traffic to a variant that isn't registered as 'served' by the dedicated pool. Router marked variant as 'compatible-fallback' -> started routing. Dedicated autoscaler saw sudden drop in active sessions for the pool and scaled down. After that, router tried again and got connection failures -> more fallbacks -> loop. Looks like routing policy and model-variant registry disagree.

oncall-alex: That explains blackholed traffic. Are we already failing over to hosted?

runtime-ryan: Some requests are being sent to hosted fallback but the router's rate limiter + policy backoff caused batching into the dedicated pool causing transient queuing. Net result: ~30s per-request spike, some 503s.

sre-kim: I’m seeing autoscaler events: `scale from 12 to 3 replicas due to low_utilization` at 12:11:03 UTC. HPA decision looks based on 'active_sessions' metric which is derived from per-router health pings. Those health pings stop when router drops the variant mapping -> circular.

oncall-maya: Marking sev=2 for now since some customers impacted but partial fallback exists. Noting @cs-jordan so CS can prepare comms.

cs-jordan: Acknowledged. I'll open a short banner and notify the top 5 tenants who hit errors. No sensitive data involved.

eng-platform-liz: Quick mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscaler (set min replicas=8) 2) temporarily disable 'cost-fallback-v2' routing policy 3) force-register the variant to dedicated pool registry if registration failed 4) scale up pool to safe capacity 10-12 replicas 5) monitor 5xx and latency. Who can run the commands?

oncall-alex: I can run the policy toggle and pause autoscaler. Ryan or Kim do you want to register variant?

runtime-ryan: I can update the model-variant registry. Steps: 
- run `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/variants/register -d '{"variant":"v2-small","pool":"dedicated-usw2"}'`
- confirm `GET /api/pools/dedicated-usw2/variants` shows v2-small

sre-kim: I'll bump the HPA min replicas: `kubectl patch hpa dedicated-pool -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":8}}'` and then scale to 10 manually: `kubectl scale deployment/dedicated-pool --replicas=10`

oncall-maya: Do we have a quick rollback if this makes things worse?

eng-platform-liz: If traffic increases error rates we'll revert policy toggle and restore original minReplicas. Also we can set router to prefer region fallback to us-east-1 hosted before dedicated pool if needed.

deploy-bot: Deploy log: policy-service v1.9.2 -> v1.9.3 rolled 10m ago in us-west-2. Modified fallback comparator logic. Change ID: PR#4821.

runtime-ryan: That PR is likely culprit — update changed variant-matching to rely on `compat_score` and didn't validate pool binding. Rolling back that change is an option but prefer hotfix: re-add strict pool binding check.

oncall-alex: I'm going to disable 'cost-fallback-v2' now. `POST /admin/policies/cost-fallback-v2/disable` -> done. (added :white_check_mark:)

sre-kim: HPA min set to 8 and scaled to 10. `kubectl get pods` shows new pods starting.

runtime-ryan: Registered v2-small to dedicated-usw2 via controlplane API and health checks passing. Router now shows variant mapping stable.

oncall-maya: Watching error rates and latency. 5xx rate dropping from 8% -> 1.2% in 2 minutes. p50 latency back to normal.

cs-jordan: Sent a short note to affected customers: "We experienced degraded inference availability in us-west-2 due to a routing policy and scaling mismatch. Traffic is now stable; we'll follow up with root cause and mitigations."

eng-platform-liz: Nice. Next steps for post-incident: - revert the fallback comparator change in PR#4821 or add extra validation - add guard in autoscaler to ignore transient zero-sessions for 60s - add telemetry that tracks variant->pool binding at router decision time - run chaos test for variant registry outages

oncall-alex: Agreed. Also creating postmortem ticket and assigning owners. I'll set severity to P2 and include timeline.

sre-kim: Logging note: we should avoid autoscaler reacting to router-internal health checks. I've added a TODO to decouple metrics.

runtime-ryan: I'll prepare the minimal hotfix for policy-service to reintroduce strict binding check and a unit test for the scenario.

oncall-maya: Wrapping up for handoff to next oncall in 30m. Any objections?

oncall-alex: No objections. Thx everyone.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=P2, incident_id=INC-20260315-09. Postmortem assigned: ENG-4821. Next update scheduled in 2h.
